newsitem.title: USA: SRW wheat tour notes little disease,near avg yield.
newsitem.headline: SRW wheat tour notes little disease,near avg yield.

text.p: Participants on one route of the third and final day of an annual U.S. soft red winter (SRW) wheat tour said they saw better-than-average quality wheat with near average potential yields and little disease.

Based on data collected after a total of five stops to inspect fields in the bootheel area of Missouri and northeast Arkansas, crop scouts estimated an average potential SRW wheat yield in those areas of 46.2 bushels per acre, ranging from 42 to 50 bushels.
The five stops were in Stoddard County, Mo., Clay County, Ark., Randolph County, Ark. and Lawrence County, Ark.

In 1996, Stoddard County produced an average yield of 48.9 bushels per acre, Clay County 48.3 bushels, Randolph County 49.0 bushels and Lawrence County 49.0 bushels per acre, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture. The average yield for those counties was 48.8 bushels per acre in 1996.
The five-year average Missouri yield from 1990 to 1994 was 40.2 bushels per acre and for Arkansas, 38.4 bushels per acre, according to U.S. Department of Agriculture data.
Participants on this route saw little disease. Most of the wheat was ripened enough to be harvested within a week to 10 days, one participant said.
In Stoddard County, crop scouts also saw little disease. Kernels were plump but cheat and wild oats, weeds that compete with wheat for moisture and nutrients, were seen.
"But if you can combine it out, it would not be a severe problem," said Ben Handcock, executive vice president of the Wheat Quality Council, the tour's sponsor.

Four vehicles with 16 people were traveling four different routes Wednesday through Missouri and Arkansas on the final leg of the SRW wheat tour. The tour ends late Wednesday in Little Rock, Ark. where Wednesday's tiller count will be calculated for Arkansas and Missouri.
